newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close higher, Telekom helps sentiment.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close higher, Telekom helps sentiment.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur shares closed higher, helped by a strong showing in the market's largest-capitalised stock Telekom Malaysia.
Small-capitalised stocks, which have been lagging the market, also firmed on the back of fresh retail interest.

"There was some profit-taking going on, but the market was holding very well. I think market sentiment was boosted by Telekom," said one dealer. Telekom rose 80 cents to 20.10 ringgit after posting a 19 percent rise in 1996 net profits.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 11.23 points at 1,270.67.
The small-capitalised Second Board index rose 14.57 points or 2.29 percent to 649.53.
Market volume was 701 million shares, with gainers leading losers 490 to 146.
The resurgence in Telekom stock helped push utility firm Tenaga Nasional up 40 cents to 11.90 ringgit.
Bolton rose 13 cents to 5.05 ringgit after announcing a 42.7 percent increase in 1996 net earnings.
Second boarders Repco, Dunham-Bush and Lityan led the gainers' list, rising between 2.25 and 3.75 ringgit.
